Package hadur2.core.policy

Class RammerPolicy

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.policy.RammerPolicy
public final class RammerPolicy extends Object
RAM-1, RAM-2: recognising a robot that is simply driving at us, and the response to it, no profile or gun tier needed.

RAM-2 (3.5) adds a second, battle-long verdict on top of RAM-1. A charge (the closing speed held for CHARGE_TICKS scans) that gets within RAM_RANGE px while both robots have more than MIN_ENERGY energy is a ram; rams in CONFIRM_ROUNDS different rounds confirm a rammer for the rest of the battle (one is not enough: XanderCat, spawned 190 px away, once drove straight through us at a round's start). From then on, escape(double, double, double, double) answers true from the second closing scan within ESCAPE_RANGE px until the enemy is more than ESCAPE_RELEASE px away, and the movement runs (move.RamEscape). The confirmation is what keeps it off strong robots: on the 3.4 benches, no top-19 robot came within 120 px on a charge with both robots above 20 energy (strong bots close in only to finish a disabled Hadur), while every rammer and close-range nano did in nearly every round. Detecting from range alone (4 scans within 500 px) also caught them, and cost up to 15 points of share against Raven.

While the enemy's own speed toward us is at CLOSING_RATE px/tick or more for TICKS scans running, within RANGE px, the response is active: fire full power (POWER), capped and gated the same way the other full-power rules are (PowerPolicy), and reverse the orbit's side rather than the one the wall-smoothed heading would otherwise pick (SurfMover). Once active, it stays active while the enemy is still within RANGE (a rammer does not stop being dangerous the one tick its closing rate dips), and clears once it backs out past that range.

The rate is the enemy's own velocity resolved onto the line from them to us, not the raw change in distance between scans: distance also moves with our own approach or retreat, and a raw delta divided by nothing is wrong whenever a scan is missed and the gap between two readings is more than one tick. Velocity is already a per-tick quantity, so no division by elapsed ticks is needed once it is used instead.

Where it sits in the tick: HadurCore calls tick(double, double) with each scan's distance and the enemy's closing speed; while it returns true, the bullet power is raised toward POWER (never past what PowerPolicy's own energy and quarter-energy caps allow) and SurfMover.setRammerActive(true) flips the no-wave orbit's chosen side. A rammer rarely gives the gun a real firing wave to surf, so the flip applies to the plain orbit, not to wave surfing itself. newRound() forgets the run.
